Overall, we hope this chapter can serve as a comprehensive guide to the various

include the required configuration steps, master data, and end-to-end process
demonstrations for each scenario, thus enabling your company to streamline its

have a better understanding of how SAP EWM can be integrated with production
planning and thus how to help your company streamline its supply chain
operations.
2.1 Overview of Production Integration
Production planning assists organizations in managing and strategizing their
manufacturing and production procedures. The module is structured to
facilitate the entire production cycle, encompassing planning, scheduling, MRP,
production execution, and monitoring.
Production planning enables organizations to create production plans and
schedules based on customer demand, sales forecasts, and available resources.
It also allows them to track and manage inventory levels, production costs, and
quality control processes.
Some key features of production planning include:
Capacity planning
This feature allows organizations to plan and manage their production
capacity to ensure that they can meet customer demand without
overburdening their resources.
Bill of materials (BOM) management
Production planning enables users to manage BOMs for their products, which
includes the list of materials required for production, as well as the quantities
and the order in which they need to be used.
MRP
Production planning uses MRP to help organizations determine what
materials are required for production and when materials need to be ordered
or produced.

Production scheduling
This feature allows users to schedule production based on available resources
and customer demand.
Integrating production with a warehouse management system (WMS) can
enhance the efficiency, accuracy, and productivity of both production and
warehouse processes. Real-time tracking of raw materials, components, and
finished products can prevent stock shortages or overstocking. Planning and
scheduling production runs becomes easier, ensuring on-time delivery of
products. Automating manual processes decreases errors and improves data
accuracy, leading to better decision-making and lower costs. Additionally,
reduced lead times and increased responsiveness to customer demands are
other benefits that can be realized. Overall, integrating production with a WMS
improves supply chain visibility and operational efficiency, resulting in increased
customer satisfaction and profitability.
By combining the production planning, materials management, and SAP EWM
modules, efficient production management can be achieved. This is possible
due to the modules providing end-to-end visibility and control over the entire
production process. The production planning module facilitates production
planning and scheduling, while the SAP EWM module covers goods receipt and
goods issue process.
By integrating production processes with SAP EWM, the precision of inventory
management has been enhanced, enabling improved tracking of raw materials,
components, and finished goods. Furthermore, it facilitates real-time monitoring
of production activities, leading to informed decision-making based on up-to-
date data. Moreover, the integration of production processes with SAP EWM
offers enhanced inventory visibility by allowing the receipt of final products
directly from production to warehouses. It also enhances the operation of
production supply areas by optimizing the staging of components and semi-
finished materials. Finally, posting the goods consumption provides improved
inventory and cost visibility.
The process of integrating production processes with SAP EWM commenced in
the early 2010s with the introduction of production integration functionality.
This enabled real-time communication between SAP EWM and other SAP
modules, including production planning and materials management. The result
was a more cohesive and integrated approach to warehouse and production
management.

SAP EWM has undergone significant evolution over the years, continuously
enhancing and adding new capabilities to better cater to the dynamic needs of
businesses in warehouse and production management. Presently, SAP EWM is
widely adopted across various industries, and its integration with production
processes remains a vital aspect of the solution.
The primary objective of integrating production and extended warehouse
management, as shown in Figure 2.1, is to facilitate the timely and efficient
staging of products, also known as production staging, from the warehouse to
the assembly line. This step also involves posting consumption for the
production process, returning unused components, and receiving finished
products into the warehouse.
Modern automated warehouses employ a variety of technologies, including
material flow systems, automated storage and retrieval systems, automated
guided vehicles (AGVs), and warehouse robotics solutions, to fulfill production
integration requirements. By leveraging these technologies, businesses can
optimize warehouse operations, lower costs, and enhance productivity,
resulting in improved business outcomes.
The integration of SAP EWM with production processes is gaining popularity in
several industries, including discrete manufacturing, process manufacturing, and
repetitive manufacturing. This integration serves various business functions,
such as transferring raw materials or semi-finished components from the
warehouse to production lines and receiving finished or semi-finished materials
from production or assembly lines to the warehouse.

To cater to the industry-specific and business-specific process needs for
producing finished goods, SAP EWM offers two production integration options

Delivery based production integration
Since the launch of SAP EWM 7.0, SAP has provided delivery-based
production integration capabilities. This feature enables the ERP system to
generate delivery documents for both the materials that require staging and
those that need to be consumed. Subsequently, SAP EWM receives these
delivery documents for material picking and consumption posting. In
essence, this methodology relies on delivery documents.
Advanced production integration
Beginning from SAP EWM 9.2, advanced production integration option has
been provided by SAP for production processes. Through this option, a
production material request (PMR) is created in SAP EWM when the ERP
system sends a message with the requisite information. This integration is
essentially founded on the concept PMR.

Some key concepts in production planning include the following:
Production supply area
A production supply area is a physical location adjacent to the production
lines where raw materials and semi-finished goods are staged. This area is
typically located in close proximity to production lines. Within SAP EWM, a
production supply area is regarded as master data.
Control cycle
A control cycle establishes the connection between the demand source, such
as a production line, and the supply source, which could be an external
supplier or warehouse.

2.2 Delivery-Based Production Integration
We’ll begin this section with a detailed overview of delivery-based production
integration. Then, we’ll dive into staging and consumption for manufacturing
orders, including the business process as well as step-by-step process
demonstrations. We’ll also discuss the goods receipt process in detail.
2.2.1 Overview
For delivery-based production integration, as shown in Figure 2.2, information
flows between the SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA system and the SAP EWM system.
Multiple deliveries can be generated for different stages, including pick parts
staging, release parts staging, and goods issue posting. Additionally, the ERP or
SAP S/4HANA system can trigger further actions.
Figure 2.2 Delivery-Based Production Integration
The benefits of integrating delivery-based production include the following:
The warehouse operation team can perform multiple tasks within the SAP
ERP system.
The warehouse can transport materials from the warehouse to the
production location in a shuttle scenario.
Moreover, they have access to the shipping functionality within SAP ERP,
which enables them to manage the shipment of goods.
The team can also utilize the Kanban functionality within SAP ERP, which is a
tool used in lean manufacturing to regulate production levels based on

customer demand.

Available for stock (AFS) storage location (one SAP EWM-managed storage

2.2.2 Staging for Manufacturing Orders
In simpler terms, staging to production refers to the process of selecting the
requested raw materials or components and delivering them to designated
supply area to production, with the help of SAP EWM. The necessary materials
for production assembly lines are stored in a warehouse, which is managed by a
team responsible for making the required components and materials available
for manufacturing orders. This process involves transferring the materials and
components from the warehouse to the production supply area and preparing
the workstations and resources necessary for the production process. This
transfer of materials from the warehouse to the production supply area is known
as the staging process in SAP EWM.
As shown in Figure 2.7, SAP EWM offers various options for staging to
production, which can be triggered by SAP EWM itself or a core system such as
SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA, or a production system such as SAP Manufacturing
Execution or SAP Digital Manufacturing.
Figure 2.7 Supported Ways of Staging

As shown in Figure 2.8, SAP provides the following staging options:
Staging for production with deliveries
Production supply with Kanban
Production supply with just-in-time (JIT)
Figure 2.8 Process Overview: Picking and Staging
In the following sections, we’ll walk through the business process for staging
production with deliveries and with one SAP EWM-managed storage location
(AFS storage location). We’ll discuss the configuration and master data for this
process and then walk you step-by-step through a process demo.
Business Process
As shown in Figure 2.9, for this business process, you would follow these high-
level steps:
A manufacturing order for both pick parts and release parts is created in
SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA.
The manufacturing order is released, and staging for individual
production orders (pick parts) is performed using Transaction CO02,
while collective staging for multiple orders (release order parts) is carried
out using Transaction MF60.
The release of the manufacturing order in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA
triggers warehouse management material staging, which can be
automated. This step also results in the creation of a production supply
delivery, which is replicated to SAP EWM.

The confirmation of the warehouse task triggers a dummy transfer

2.2.3 Consumption for Manufacturing Orders
In this section, we’ll delve deeply into the delivery-based consumption for
manufacturing orders. At a high level, the trigger for the consumption of
components for a process order is initiated from SAP ERP. After a process order is
confirmed, an outbound delivery is created in SAP ERP, which is then replicated
to SAP EWM. This delivery is not relevant for picking, and with the correct
settings, the system posts the goods issue for the outbound delivery. We’ll start
with an overview of the business process and then get into a process demo.
Business Process
As shown in Figure 2.36, the consumption process follows these steps:
1. An SAP ERP system automatically generates a consumption posting delivery
during the confirmation of the manufacturing order.
© 

85
2. This delivery is then replicated to the SAP EWM system. Note that the
outbound delivery order in the SAP EWM system is not needed for picking as
the system posts goods issue as soon as the outbound delivery order is
created.
3. Additionally, the system determines the goods movement bin based on the
assignment of the production supply area to the storage bin.
4. As soon as the goods issue posting is triggered from SAP EWM, this step
updates the goods issue posting or the material document for
manufacturing order with movement type 261.
Figure 2.36 Consumption for Manufacturing Order

Once PMRs are created, your warehouse operations teams can work
independently of SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA.

2.3.1 Staging for Manufacturing Orders
In this section, we’ll delve into staging for manufacturing orders in advanced
production integration processes, which involves the preparation and gathering
of materials required for production. This phase includes activities such as
creating PMRs from the warehouse and transferring them to the production
area. Staging ensures that all necessary components are available when needed,
thus optimizing the production process and minimizing delays.
Business Process
Business warehouses utilize a staging process to supply materials, whether
packed or unpacked, to production and then consume these materials during
the production process. To ensure that materials are supplied as needed and to
prevent delays, the staging process is planned systematically with the help of
advanced production integration in SAP EWM. When staging requires a large
© 

97
quantity or a significant amount of manufacturing time, production can occur
either with the full requested quantity or with partial quantities, HU after HU.
This approach also maximizes the utilization of space in the production supply
area.
As shown in Figure 2.56, with advanced production integration, the SAP ERP or
SAP S/4HANA system automatically creates a PMR in SAP EWM when a
manufacturing order is released. This PMR triggers the warehouse management
material staging process, which can be done manually or automatically.
Figure 2.56 Material Staging for Production
In SAP EWM, the Transaction /SCWM/STAGE (Schedule Staging for Production)
can be used to create a staging warehouse task. This transaction can be
executed manually or as a background job with input parameters such as
warehouse, production staging area, and staging method.
If a user needs to select a specific PMR and stage materials accordingly, the Web
Dynpro user interface (UI) Transaction NWBC can be used to provide more
flexibility and enable a user to view the stock overview in the production supply
area.
In advanced production integration, SAP EWM provides several options for
staging materials, including the following:
Single-order staging
In this staging approach, the system generates a warehouse task for each line
item in a PMR to move the product to the production supply area, as shown in
Figure 2.57. Each warehouse task is linked to a single PMR, and once
confirmed, the task is associated with the specific PMR item. The material and
batch consumption posting can be done for the same PMR. If a HU or material

98
is not required for production, the user can manually release the PMR item
reference for stock. The single-order staging method enables the staging of
products for a particular PMR or for a PMR with unique characteristics. For
example, products can be staged from a specific batch for a particular PMR.
Figure 2.57 Single-Order Staging
Cross-order staging
In this material staging method, the system accumulates material from
multiple PMRs and generates a warehouse task to move the material together.
The warehouse task created in this method is not linked to any specific PMR
item. After the warehouse task is confirmed, it does not have any reference to
a PMR item. Consumption posting for material and batch can be posted for
the PMR that has an item for the material and batch. This method offers
flexibility since warehouse users can stage products for a single PMR or for
several PMRs.
To maintain a minimum quantity of the product on the production supply
area, the bin assignment is used. If the sum of the quantity in the production
supply area and open warehouse task quantity is less than the minimum
quantity, the system generates a warehouse task to move the replenishment
quantity to the production supply area. The replenishment quantity is also
maintained in the bin assignment.
In addition to single-order staging and cross-order staging, you also have the
option for part replenishment creation or to use no order staging at all, but these
methods are not as widely used so they will not be covered in depth here.

3 Quality Management
Quality management is a pivotal component of SAP S/4HANA that enables
businesses to implement and operate quality control processes with ease. It is
crafted to prevent defects, foster continuous process improvement, and establish
sustainable quality control programs. The aim of this chapter is to provide you
with a comprehensive guide to various quality management processes and their
seamless integration with SAP Extended Warehouse Management (SAP EWM),
especially with embedded Extended Warehouse Management in SAP S/4HANA
(embedded EWM).
SAP EWM has the ability to integrate with quality management in order to guarantee
adherence to quality standards during the storage and handling of goods.
Organizations can reap numerous benefits from quality management, including
compliance with manufacturing quality regulations, reduced operating costs, and
enhanced customer satisfaction. The integration between SAP EWM and quality
management allows for quality inspections to be conducted at various stages of the
warehouse process, such as during goods receipt, putaway, and outbound processes.
The result of this integration is the assurance that quality standards are met prior to
the dispatch of products to customers. SAP EWM can activate quality inspections and
apprise quality management of the outcomes, thereby allowing quality management
to create quality notifications or update inspection lots. The integration also facilitates
the monitoring of quality-related data throughout the warehouse process, granting
organizations visibility into quality-related key performance indicators (KPIs) and
enabling data-driven decisions.
This chapter examines various aspects of quality management integration and
different quality management business processes that can be integrated with SAP
EWM. The introductory section provides a synopsis of quality management in SAP
EWM, followed by an analysis of different quality management processes such as the
inspection of material and batch during an inbound delivery in SAP. This process is
further categorized into the inspection of material for externally procured and in-house
inspection.
Furthermore, this chapter delves into another quality management process, internal
warehouse inspection, which is further divided into stock inspection and recurring
inspection for batches. Finally, this chapter provides in-depth coverage of the advanced
returns management process with quality inspection.
